extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for the NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks track
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers (and implicitly authors) evaluating submissions to the NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks track, covering dataset quality, benchmark reproducibility, ethical concerns, reviewer responsibilities, and scoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether there is sufficient detail on data collection and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the submission describes how data were collected, curated, labeled, and organized so that others can understand provenance and structure. (From 'For Datasets: Reviewers should assess whether there is sufficient detail on: Data collection and organization')

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether there is sufficient detail on availability and maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the dataset will be accessible to others now and in the long term, and whether there is a realistic plan for hosting and maintenance. (From 'For Datasets: ... Availability and maintenance')

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and responsible use
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether there is sufficient detail on ethical and responsible use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ethical sourcing, consent, privacy protections, potential harms, and guidance for responsible use. Flag ethical concerns for an ethics review if appropriate. (From 'For Datasets: ... Ethical and responsible use' and 'Ethical Review' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and intended uses (required for dataset submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset submissions should include documentation and intended uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide documentation describing the dataset and recommended/intended uses so reviewers (and future users) can understand scope, limitations, and appropriate applications. (From 'Dataset submissions should include: Documentation and intended uses')

rubrics_metrics.name: URL for reviewer access
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset submissions should include a URL for reviewer access to the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a link that allows reviewers to access the dataset (noting that hosted datasets may complicate anonymity). This is required to enable evaluation. (From 'Dataset submissions should include: A URL for reviewer access to the dataset')

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting, licensing and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset submissions should include a hosting, licensing and maintenance plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe where the dataset will be hosted, what license governs reuse, and plans for long-term maintenance and updates. This addresses accessibility and sustainability concerns. (From 'Dataset submissions should include: A hosting, licensing and maintenance plan')

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark reproducibility detail
rubrics_metrics.description: For Benchmarks: reviewers should evaluate whether there is sufficient detail to support reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that benchmark definitions, evaluation protocols, data splits, metrics, baselines, and code/instructions are sufficiently specified so others can reproduce results. (From 'For Benchmarks: Reviewers should evaluate whether there is sufficient detail to support reproducibility')

rubrics_metrics.name: Special submission mode / single-blind allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Datasets and Benchmarks track, authors can choose to submit single-blind since it may be impossible to share hosted and well-documented datasets entirely anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware that submissions may be single-blind and that anonymity constraints are acknowledged by the track. This affects expectations around hosted data and reviewer handling of identifying information. (From 'Special Submission Mode' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (reviewer input required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single overall assessment score for the submission as required by the review process. (From 'Reviewer Scoring: Reviewers must provide: An "overall score"')

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (reviewer input required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate your confidence in the evaluation (how well you could assess the submission) as required by the review process. (From 'Reviewer Scoring: ... A "confidence score"')

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues flagging and ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with a paper, reviewers should flag it for an ethics review and reference the NeurIPS ethics guidelines for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ethical concerns arise (e.g., privacy, consent, potential harms), flag the submission for a formal ethics review and consult NeurIPS ethics guidelines to determine appropriateness. (From 'Ethical Review' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep reviews confidential (reviewer responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep everything relating to the review process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose review content, reviewer identities, or submission material outside the review process. Confidentiality is a strict reviewer responsibility. (From 'Reviewer Responsibilities' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use ideas/code/results prior to public release
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in their own work until they become publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incorporating or acting on privileged information from submissions; wait until the work is publicly released. (From 'Reviewer Responsibilities' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not share submissions without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not talk about or share submissions with anyone without prior approval from the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain explicit permission from program chairs before discussing or distributing submission materials. (From 'Reviewer Responsibilities' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on documentation and accessibility (distinct from main track)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Datasets & Benchmarks track places more emphasis on documentation and accessibility than the main NeurIPS track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating submissions, weigh high-quality documentation and ease of access more heavily than in the main track. (From 'Distinct from Main Track' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on long-term maintenance and licensing (distinct from main track)
rubrics_metrics.description: The track places more emphasis on long-term maintenance and licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plans for sustainable hosting, maintenance schedules, and appropriate licensing as key quality indicators. (From 'Distinct from Main Track' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on ethical sourcing of data (distinct from main track)
rubrics_metrics.description: The track places more emphasis on ethical sourcing of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate provenance, consent, and ethical collection practices more strongly than in main-track evaluations. (From 'Distinct from Main Track' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on community impact (will the dataset/benchmark be widely used?)
rubrics_metrics.description: The track places more emphasis on community impact — whether the dataset/benchmark will be widely used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider potential adoption, generality, and usefulness to the broader community as part of the evaluation. (From 'Distinct from Main Track' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Less emphasis on novel ML methods (distinct from main track)
rubrics_metrics.description: The track places less emphasis on novel ML methods compared to the main track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize submissions for lack of novel algorithms if they provide high-quality data/benchmarks; focus evaluation on dataset/benchmark quality, documentation, ethics, and reproducibility. (From 'Distinct from Main Track' section.)
